# Identity client + recipes

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P2 · Proven identity](../README.md#phase-2--proven-identity) · **Lane:** Agent / harness · **Label:** `feature:identity-client` · **Epic:** [#116](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/116) · **Tickets:** 6 (3S 3M)

Extends the P1 `warden identity` client with agent keys and the RFC 8693 token exchange, extends the P1 loopback forwarder from W-P1-IDC-04 into `warden identity forward` for sidecar containers and adds agent tokens to the P1 `warden identity exec` for laptops and CI, and ships Claude Code and Codex CLI compose recipes behind a require-mode worker. The agent container never holds the agent key, the Dex refresh token, a Warden token or a real vendor API key: a separate sidecar holds the identity material and the worker swaps placeholder API keys. Everything is new and opt-in; existing recipes, `run`, `control-plane` and the P1 identity commands are unchanged.

## How we build it

- Commands. All new commands live in the `identity` cobra subtree that W-P1-IDC-02 adds under the `warden` root (cmd/proxy/root.go `Use: "warden"`); there is no separate `warden-identity` tool and no `proxy identity exec`. They reuse internal/identityclient from W-P1-IDC-02: the same config precedence (flags, WARDEN_IDENTITY_*, identity.yaml), shared cache, lock file and `--client-id` default `warden-cli`. New: `enroll` (agent key) and `forward` (long-lived forwarder for a sidecar container). `exec` (forwarder on loopback plus a child process) ships in P1 as W-P1-IDC-04; P2 adds `--agent-id` and `--run-as` to it. `token` and `status` gain `--agent-id`. New env vars: WARDEN_IDENTITY_TOKEN_ENDPOINT, WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_ID, WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_KEY_FILE, WARDEN_IDENTITY_CP_CA.
- Agent key. `warden identity enroll --agent-id <id> [--key-file PATH] [--force]` generates an Ed25519 key with crypto/ed25519 and writes it as PKCS#8 PEM to a 0600 file in a 0700 directory (default `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/agents/<id>.key`), by temp file, fsync and rename. It refuses to overwrite without --force and refuses a key file readable by group or others, as the P1 cache does. It prints only the public JWK (kty OKP, crv Ed25519, alg EdDSA, kid = RFC 7638 thumbprint computed with internal/keys from W-P2-KEYS-01, no `d`), which W-P2-AREG-02 and the offline CLI from p2-agent-registry accept as-is. Agent keys are per harness deployment (one sidecar fleet), not per user machine: the registry holds at most 2 keys per agent, so rotation is enroll a new key, register it, switch the sidecar, then remove the old key.
- Subject token. By default it comes from the P1 Client.Token() path (refresh at 2/3 of lifetime with the refresh token, never prompts). `--subject-token-file PATH` (must be 0600, re-read before each exchange) supports harness platforms that obtain the user's ID token themselves and the CI smoke path through scripts/dex-token.sh. No new code path ever starts a device-code prompt except `warden identity login` and an `exec` run attached to a terminal. On ErrLoginRequired the forwarder keeps serving the current Warden token until it expires, then refuses new tunnels with reason login_required until the user runs `warden identity login` against the same cache.
- Exchange. `Client.Exchange` POSTs form-encoded to the CP `/oauth2/token` (W-P2-TOKX-03) with grant_type token-exchange, subject_token_type id_token, audience=warden-worker, optional scope, and a private_key_jwt assertion (header alg EdDSA plus kid; claims iss=sub=agent id, aud=exactly `--token-endpoint`, iat, exp=iat+60s, 128-bit random jti; a new assertion per request, meeting W-P2-TOKX-01). The token endpoint has no implied default. CP TLS is verified against `--cp-ca` (the proxy CA in compose). The Warden token is held only in memory and never written to disk. Re-exchange starts at 2/3 of expires_in measured from local receipt time, with up to 10% random jitter, single-flighted. On network errors it retries with jittered exponential backoff (1s to 60s) while the current token is valid; on 429 it honours Retry-After. invalid_client, unauthorized_client and invalid_grant map to ErrExchangeDenied{Code} (exit 4); only the RFC 6749 error code is surfaced, never the response body. Without `--agent-id` no exchange happens and the forwarder injects the P1 Dex ID token, so the forwarder also works against P1 attribute-mode workers.
- Forwarder rules (security-critical, in internal/identityclient/forwarder.go, added in P1 by W-P1-IDC-04 and extended here): it accepts only CONNECT and answers any other method with 405 without forwarding; it reads the CONNECT header block with a 32 KiB and 100-line cap and a 10s deadline (matching the W-P1-VRFY-02 worker limits); it drops any Proxy-Authorization sent by the client and injects `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` (Contract v1); it dials only the single configured `--worker` address and never resolves or dials the CONNECT target; it relays the worker's status line and headers verbatim, including 403 and 407 with Proxy-Authenticate; with no valid token it answers 503 with header `X-Warden-Forwarder-Reason: login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied` and never dials the worker; it caps concurrent tunnels (`--max-tunnels`, default 512, then 503).
- Token rotation and long tunnels. Each tunnel snapshots the token and its exp at CONNECT. The worker re-checks CONNECT identity expiry on every terminated request (W-P1-VRFY-02), so after a rotation the forwarder drains old tunnels: a draining tunnel is closed after 2s with no bytes in either direction, and at the latest at its token's exp. New CONNECTs always carry the newest token. This bounds how long any tunnel outlives a block, an agent disable or a key removal to the token lifetime (at most 15m for an exchanged token), with no separate max-age flag; the worker enforces the same bound by closing require-mode tunnels at exp plus skew (W-P2-WBND-09), and the client's next CONNECT carries the newest token. A 407 from the worker triggers one forced refresh and one retry of the CONNECT before the 407 is relayed.
- Recipe topology (isolation preserved). The agent container joins only `<agent>-internal` (internal: true) and gets HTTPS_PROXY=http://warden-identity:3128 with no credentials. The `warden-identity` sidecar runs `warden identity forward --agent-id <id> --listen 0.0.0.0:3128 --worker warden:8080` and joins `<agent>-internal` and cp-net; it keeps the agent key and the identity cache on its own named volume, which is never mounted into the agent. The worker joins `<agent>-internal`, egress and cp-net. Dex and LDAP come from deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml (W-P1-DEX-02) and the CP from docker-compose.control-plane.yml (per-worker tokens from W-P1-WTOK-06, or worker certs once W-P2-WCA-06 moves that recipe), run with `--policy-store=versioned --bundles=require` and a CP config with `keys.enabled: true` and a `tokenService:` block; the bootstrap exports the bundle JWKS (`warden control-plane keys export --purpose bundle`) to a volume the worker pins through `controlPlane.bundleKeysFile`; neither is ever attached to the agent network. The forwarder adds no egress route because it only connects to the worker. `exec` (W-P1-IDC-04, extended by W-P2-RCP-06) is documented as the laptop and CI option: it keeps tokens out of the child's env, argv and logs, but a same-uid child can read the key and cache unless `--run-as` is used.
- Agent identity at the worker. Each recipe worker is started with `warden run --agent-id <id>` (the worker binding from W-P2-AREG-05; `central.agentID` is the YAML form), so the worker's agent id equals the registry id. Without it, internal/worker/judge.go defaultAgentID falls back to `agent:<port>` from agentid.PortBindingIdentifier and W-P2-WBND-02's act check could never match. The served policy also carries exactly one `agents` entry with that id and `identity: require` (W-P2-WBND-03).
- Vendor credentials. The agent gets placeholder keys only (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=anthropic_secret_001, OPENAI_API_KEY=openai_secret_001), and a recipe worker config maps each placeholder with `secrets: [{placeholder, envVar}]` as configs/config.example-worker.yaml does today, so the real key is set only on the worker container. Subscription logins (Claude.ai sign-in for Claude Code, ChatGPT sign-in for Codex) are unsupported in these recipes, because they would put real OAuth credentials in the agent's home directory.
- Registration. A one-shot `identity-bootstrap` service enrolls the sidecar key if none exists and registers the agent with the offline `warden control-plane agent register --state-dir` CLI from p2-agent-registry (allowed group `eng` from the W-P1-DEX-02 LDAP seed), and is idempotent on a second `up`. The docs also show the console path (W-P2-AREG-02) for production. Warden services in the new recipes build from the repo Dockerfile (`build: {context: ../.., dockerfile: Dockerfile}`), because the published `ethosagent/warden:0.3.0` image does not contain the new subcommands.
- Degraded modes, documented in docs/recipes. CP down: traffic continues until the current Warden token expires (at most 15m), then new tunnels get 503 cp_unreachable. Dex down: subject refresh fails; exchange continues while the cached ID token is valid (at most 1h), then login_required. Sidecar restart: re-exchanges from the cached subject token (Warden tokens are memory-only). Clock skew: more than `identity.clockSkewSeconds` (default 60s) breaks worker verification (W-P2-WBND-01) and more than 60s breaks the assertion, so NTP is required. Disabled agent or removed key: new tunnels are refused at the worker; old tunnels end at token exp at the latest.
- Observability. Structured stderr logs only: event=tunnel_open, tunnel_close (target host:port, worker status, bytes, duration, 8-hex sha256 token fingerprint), event=token_rotated (fingerprint, exp, draining count), event=exchange (outcome, RFC error code) and event=login_required. Optional `--health-listen` (off by default; on cp-net in the recipes) serves GET /healthz returning `{"state":"valid|expiring|login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied","exp":...}` without the token. Tokens, assertions, nonces, Proxy-Authorization values, key material and IdP or CP response bodies never appear in logs, errors or argv. Worker decision events carry user_sub and identity_status (W-P1-VRFY-03) plus the act and sid fields from W-P2-WBND-02, and the CP traffic API `/dashboard/api/traffic?user=` (W-P1-VRFY-04) is the attribution check.
- Back-compat. Everything is new and opt-in. The existing recipes (ethos, hermes, openclaw, zeroclaw), `run`, `control-plane`, the P1 identity commands, cache format and exit codes 2 and 3 are unchanged; exit code 4 is new. docs/identity-contract.md gets a P2 addendum describing `forward` and `exec` as the replacement for the P1 token-in-HTTPS_PROXY limitation, with no change to any v1 header or claim.
- Isolation proof. scripts/recipe-isolation.sh <claude-code|codex>, run only through `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes` (no Docker in the default run), proves from inside the agent container: direct egress fails; dex:5556 and control-plane:7070 are unreachable and the identity volume is not mounted; a plain-HTTP request to the forwarder gets 405; a child-supplied Proxy-Authorization is replaced; the agent's env and $HOME hold no JWT, agent key or non-placeholder vendor key; a request through the forwarder is recorded with the seeded user's user_sub and act=<agent id>; a non-allowed host is denied; and after the agent is disabled with the offline CLI a new CONNECT is refused. A probe container on the worker network proves a CONNECT with no token gets 407. All logs contain zero JWT-shaped strings.

## Done when

From a clean clone, following only docs/recipes/claude-code.md and docs/recipes/codex.md, each compose recipe (merged with docker-compose.control-plane.yml and docker-compose.identity.yml) starts the CP with signed bundles, the key manager and the token service, Dex and LDAP, a worker started with `--agent-id` and require mode, the `warden-identity` sidecar, a bootstrap that enrolls and registers the agent idempotently, and the agent container on an internal-only network. A headless run (`claude -p` or `codex exec`) reaches its vendor API only through the sidecar and the worker, and the worker decision and the CP traffic API show the logged-in user's user_sub and act=claude-code or act=codex; with only the placeholder key the upstream 401 is the expected result, and with the real key set on the worker only the prompt completes (manual step). The agent container holds only placeholder keys and no Warden token, Dex token or agent key, and `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes` passes for both recipes, including direct-egress, CP/Dex-unreachable, no-token 407, forwarder-misuse, agent-disabled and no-token-in-logs checks.

### 1/6 · W-P2-RCP-01

**Extend internal/identityclient with agent keys and token exchange**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#117](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/117)

Extend internal/identityclient (W-P1-IDC-02) with Ed25519 agent keys, private_key_jwt assertions and the RFC 8693 exchange against the CP `/oauth2/token`, plus a Warden token source that refreshes at 2/3 of the token lifetime and never prompts. Add `warden identity enroll` and an `--agent-id` mode for `token` and `status`. This is the client half of the P2 identity flow; it changes no worker or CP code and does nothing unless the new flags are used.

**Requirements**

- `warden identity enroll --agent-id <id> [--key-file PATH] [--force]` validates the id with agentid.ValidID (p2-agent-registry), writes a PKCS#8 PEM Ed25519 key to a 0600 file in a 0700 directory (default `<os.UserConfigDir()>/warden/agents/<id>.key`) by temp file, fsync and rename, refuses an existing file without --force, and prints only the public JWK (kty OKP, crv Ed25519, alg EdDSA, kid = RFC 7638 thumbprint from internal/keys, no `d`). A key file readable by group or others is refused with an error naming the path.
- Assertion: header alg EdDSA with kid; claims iss=sub=agent id, aud=exactly the configured token endpoint, iat=now, exp=iat+60s, jti=128-bit crypto/rand base64url. A new assertion is built for every exchange, so it meets W-P2-TOKX-01 (exp-iat<=5m, single-use jti).
- Exchange: POST form-encoded to `--token-endpoint` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_TOKEN_ENDPOINT (required, no implied default) with grant_type token-exchange, subject_token_type id_token, client_assertion_type jwt-bearer, audience=warden-worker and optional `--scope`. CP TLS is trusted through `--cp-ca` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_CP_CA. `--agent-id` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_ID and `--agent-key-file` / WARDEN_IDENTITY_AGENT_KEY_FILE select the agent.
- Subject token: from the P1 Client.Token() (shared cache, lock file, `--client-id` default `warden-cli`), or from `--subject-token-file PATH` (0600 required, re-read before each exchange) for harness platforms and CI.
- New WardenTokenSource: holds the Warden token in memory only, never on disk; re-exchanges at 2/3 of expires_in from local receipt time with up to 10% jitter; single-flights concurrent callers; retries network errors with jittered backoff from 1s to 60s while the current token is valid; honours Retry-After on 429; exposes OnRotate(func()) for the forwarder.
- Errors: ErrLoginRequired from the subject source never prompts and the current Warden token is served until its exp. invalid_client, unauthorized_client and invalid_grant map to new ErrExchangeDenied{Code} (exit 4); CP unreachable with no valid token is exit 3; login required stays exit 2. Only the RFC 6749 error code is surfaced, never a response body.
- `warden identity token --agent-id <id>` prints a valid Warden token on stdout for harnesses that do not use the forwarder; `warden identity status --agent-id <id>` prints sub, act.sub, cnf.jkt, scope and exp, never the token. `--verbose` logs only outcome, error code, exp, agent id and an 8-hex sha256 fingerprint.
- Uses only the Go standard library and internal/keys for JOSE work; no new third-party dependency. P1 commands, the cache format and exit codes 2 and 3 are unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/identityclient/agentkey.go: GenerateAgentKey, SaveAgentKey and LoadAgentKey (PKCS#8 PEM, reusing the W-P1-IDC-02 permission check and atomic write helper) and PublicJWK built with the internal/keys JWK marshal and thumbprint (W-P2-KEYS-01).
2. New internal/identityclient/assertion.go: SignClientAssertion(key, kid, agentID, tokenURL, now) returning a compact EdDSA JWT with a random jti.
3. New internal/identityclient/exchange.go: Client.Exchange(ctx, subject, scope) with a dedicated http.Client (Proxy nil, `--cp-ca` root pool, 10s timeout, 64 KiB response cap), RFC 6749 error parsing into ErrExchangeDenied and ErrRateLimited{RetryAfter}.
4. New internal/identityclient/wardensource.go: WardenTokenSource wrapping either Client.Token() or a subject-token file, with the 2/3 schedule, jitter, singleflight, backoff and OnRotate hooks; clock injected for tests.
5. New cmd/proxy/identity_enroll.go registered on the W-P1-IDC-02 `identity` subtree; extend the existing token and status commands with `--agent-id`, `--agent-key-file`, `--token-endpoint`, `--cp-ca`, `--subject-token-file` and `--scope`, plus the env vars, and map ErrExchangeDenied to exit 4.
6. Tests in internal/identityclient against httptest fakes for the issuer and the CP: TestEnrollAgentKey, TestClientAssertion, TestExchangeRefreshAtTwoThirds, TestExchangeLoginRequiredNoPrompt, TestExchangeErrors; in cmd/proxy: TestIdentityExitCodes and TestIdentityEnrollAndTokenNoLeak.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestEnrollAgentKey` passes: the key file is 0600 in a 0700 directory, a second enroll without --force fails, a key chmodded to 0644 is refused with an error naming the path, and the printed JWK has kty OKP, crv Ed25519, kid equal to its RFC 7638 thumbprint and no `d` member.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestClientAssertion` verifies the assertion with the public JWK: alg EdDSA, iss=sub=agent id, aud equal to the token endpoint byte for byte, exp-iat=60s, and 1000 builds give 1000 distinct jti values.
- [ ] With a fake CP returning expires_in=900 and a fake clock, `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExchangeRefreshAtTwoThirds -race` shows one exchange at start, the next no earlier than 540s and no later than 600s, and two concurrent callers sharing one request.
- [ ] When the fake issuer's refresh returns invalid_grant, `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExchangeLoginRequiredNoPrompt` shows ErrLoginRequired with nothing written to the prompt writer, and the still-valid Warden token is served until its exp.
- [ ] Given the fake CP returns 401 invalid_client, 400 invalid_grant and 429 with Retry-After: 3, `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestExchangeErrors` maps them to ErrExchangeDenied{invalid_client}, ErrExchangeDenied{invalid_grant} and a retry no earlier than 3s, and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExitCodes` sees exit 4 for a denial.
- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityEnrollAndTokenNoLeak` runs enroll, `token --agent-id` and `status --agent-id` with `--verbose`; stderr and slog output contain no substring of the subject token, assertion, Warden token or key seed, and the token appears only on stdout of `token`.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including the coverage gate and govulncheck.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-IDC-02`](identity-contract.md#24--w-p1-idc-02) Add `warden identity` CLI for login, token, status and proxy env; [`W-P2-KEYS-01`](key-management.md#17--w-p2-keys-01) Add internal/keys Signer, JWK and RFC 7638 kid helpers; [`W-P2-TOKX-03`](token-exchange.md#37--w-p2-tokx-03) Mount POST /oauth2/token with RFC 8693 request parsing and config

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-RCP-02`](identity-client.md#26--w-p2-rcp-02) Add the token-injecting forwarder and `warden identity forward`

### 2/6 · W-P2-RCP-02

**Add the token-injecting forwarder and `warden identity forward`**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#118](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/118)

Extend the P1 CONNECT-only loopback forwarder from W-P1-IDC-04 (internal/identityclient/forwarder.go), which injects the current token as `Proxy-Authorization: Basic session:<token>` on the CONNECT to the worker, with rotation drain, a tunnel cap, client credentials, health and reason-coded 503s, and add the long-lived `warden identity forward` command that runs it as a sidecar container. Child CLIs read HTTPS_PROXY once at start, so the forwarder lets tokens rotate without restarting the agent and keeps every token out of the agent container. It adds no egress route: it only ever connects to the one configured worker.

**Requirements**

- `warden identity forward --listen <addr> --worker host:port [--agent-id ID] [--max-tunnels N] [--health-listen addr] [--client-credential-env NAME]` in the W-P1-IDC-02 `identity` subtree. `--listen` and `--worker` are required; a non-loopback `--listen` logs one startup warning. With `--agent-id` the injected token comes from WardenTokenSource (W-P2-RCP-01); without it the P1 Dex ID token from Client.Token() is injected.
- The forwarder accepts only CONNECT and answers any other method with 405 without forwarding. It reads the CONNECT header block with a 32 KiB and 100-line cap and a 10s read deadline (431 on overflow), drops any client Proxy-Authorization, and sends `CONNECT host:port` to the worker with `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)`.
- It dials only the configured `--worker` address (10s dial timeout) and never resolves or dials the CONNECT target. It relays the worker's status line and headers verbatim, including 403 and 407 with Proxy-Authenticate, then splices bytes both ways with a pooled 32 KiB buffer per direction.
- With no valid token it answers 503 with `X-Warden-Forwarder-Reason: login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied` and makes no dial to the worker. Above `--max-tunnels` (default 512) it answers 503. On a 407 from the worker it forces one token refresh and retries the CONNECT once before relaying the 407.
- Rotation: the current token is held in an atomic pointer and each tunnel snapshots the token and exp at CONNECT. After a rotation old tunnels drain: each is closed after 2s with no bytes in either direction, and at the latest at its token's exp. New CONNECTs always carry the newest token.
- `--client-credential-env NAME` (optional) requires clients to send that env var's value as the Proxy-Authorization password and answers 407 otherwise; the value is never forwarded to the worker. `--health-listen` (off by default) serves GET /healthz with the state enum valid|expiring|login_required|cp_unreachable|exchange_denied and exp, never the token.
- Logs are structured stderr events only: tunnel_open, tunnel_close (target host:port, worker status, bytes, duration, 8-hex token fingerprint), token_rotated, exchange and login_required (logged once per transition). No token, credential or Proxy-Authorization value is ever logged.
- New command only; `run`, `control-plane`, the P1 identity commands and the worker are unchanged. CONNECT setup overhead on loopback stays under 2ms per tunnel, excluding the worker.

**Implementation plan**

1. Extend internal/identityclient/forwarder.go from W-P1-IDC-04: add MaxTunnels, Clock, the reason-coded 503s and the 407 retry to Forwarder, and replace the copy loop with the pooled splice; keep the P1 header reader, single worker dial and verbatim status relay.
2. New internal/identityclient/tunnels.go: a tunnel registry recording token fingerprint, exp and last-activity per tunnel; on OnRotate it marks old tunnels draining and a ticker closes idle-for-2s or expired tunnels.
3. New internal/identityclient/health.go: the optional /healthz handler reading the WardenTokenSource state.
4. New cmd/proxy/identity_forward.go: builds the token source from W-P2-RCP-01 flags, listens, runs the forwarder until SIGTERM or SIGINT, then closes the listener and drains tunnels for up to 5s.
5. Tests in internal/identityclient with an httptest CONNECT listener as the fake worker: TestForwarderInjectsAndStrips, TestForwarderOnlyDialsWorker, TestForwarderRotationDrain (fake clock), TestForwarderNoTokenFailsClosed, TestForwarderRetryOn407, TestForwarderClientCredential, and BenchmarkForwarderConnect.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderInjectsAndStrips` shows the fake worker receives `Proxy-Authorization: Basic base64("session:"+token)` even when the client sent its own, a GET gets 405, and an oversized CONNECT header block gets 431.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderOnlyDialsWorker` uses a recording dialer and shows CONNECTs to five different targets produce dials to the worker address only.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/identityclient -run TestForwarderRotationDrain -race` with a fake clock shows a tunnel opened before a rotation keeps streaming while active, is closed 2s after it goes idle and no later than its token's exp, and a CONNECT made after the rotation carries the new token.

### 3/6 · W-P2-RCP-03

**Add the Claude Code compose recipe and docs**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#119](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/119)

Add a Claude Code recipe that runs the agent on an internal-only network, the `warden-identity` sidecar holding the agent key and identity cache, and a require-mode worker bound to agent id `claude-code`. The agent holds only a placeholder Anthropic key that the worker swaps, so no real credential or token reaches it. This is the reference recipe that W-P2-RCP-04 copies.

**Requirements**

- New deploy/compose/docker-compose.claude-code.yml, used as `-f docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f docker-compose.identity.yml -f docker-compose.claude-code.yml`. Services: the CP with `--state-dir`, `--policy-store=versioned` and `--bundles=require` (W-P2-SBND-02) and a CP config with `keys.enabled: true` (W-P2-KEYS-02) and an enabled `tokenService:` block (W-P2-TOKX-03; there is no CLI flag), using the worker auth that docker-compose.control-plane.yml sets up (no WARDEN_CP_TOKEN); a worker started with `warden run --agent-id claude-code` (W-P2-AREG-05) that pins the exported bundle JWKS through `controlPlane.bundleKeysFile`, on `claude-code-internal`, egress and cp-net; `warden-identity` running `warden identity forward --agent-id claude-code --listen 0.0.0.0:3128 --worker warden:8080` on `claude-code-internal` and cp-net with its own `identity-claude-code` volume; and `claude-code` on `claude-code-internal` only (`internal: true`) with `init: true`.
- New deploy/compose/claude-code/Dockerfile: node base image pinned by tag and digest, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` at an exact version at least two weeks old, non-root user. Agent env: HTTPS_PROXY=http://warden-identity:3128, NO_PROXY=localhost,127.0.0.1,::1, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/etc/warden/certs/proxy-ca.crt, NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1, DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1 and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=anthropic_secret_001. The implementer confirms each variable name against the pinned release and records it in the doc.
- New configs/config.recipe-claude-code-worker.yaml maps placeholder anthropic_secret_001 to envVar ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the real key is passed only to the worker container (`${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}`). New configs/config.cp-served.claude-code.yaml is default-deny, allows only api.anthropic.com:443, and has exactly one `agents` entry with id `claude-code` and `identity: require`.
- New one-shot `identity-bootstrap` service: runs `warden identity enroll --agent-id claude-code` on the sidecar volume only when no key exists, then `warden control-plane agent register --state-dir` (W-P2-AREG-06) with the public JWK and `--groups eng`, and exports the bundle JWKS with `warden control-plane keys export --purpose bundle` (W-P2-KEYS-05) into a volume the worker mounts read-only; a second `up` makes no new rows. The sidecar and worker wait on it with `condition: service_completed_successfully`.
- Warden services build from the repo Dockerfile (`build: {context: ../.., dockerfile: Dockerfile}`), because `ethosagent/warden:0.3.0` lacks the new subcommands. Third-party images are pinned by tag and digest. The agent never mounts the identity volume, the agent key or the CA key.
- New docs/recipes/claude-code.md: prerequisites, cert generation with scripts/gen-certs.sh, bootstrap, interactive login (`docker compose run --rm warden-identity identity login`), the dev path with scripts/dex-token.sh into `--subject-token-file`, running `claude` and `claude -p`, reading attribution (worker log user_sub and act, CP traffic API `?user=`), degraded modes, troubleshooting (x509, 407 reasons, 503 reasons), the threat model, and a statement that Claude.ai subscription sign-in is unsupported. Add a row to docs/recipes/README.md.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write configs/config.cp-served.claude-code.yaml and configs/config.recipe-claude-code-worker.yaml from the existing config.cp-served.yaml and config.recipe-worker.yaml.
2. Write deploy/compose/claude-code/Dockerfile and deploy/compose/docker-compose.claude-code.yml with the networks, volumes, bootstrap ordering and build contexts above.
3. Add a short deploy/compose/claude-code/bootstrap.sh run by the `identity-bootstrap` service that enrolls when the key is missing and registers when the agent is missing.
4. Write docs/recipes/claude-code.md and add the docs/recipes/README.md row.
5. Add test/deploy/recipe_claude_code_test.go (TestClaudeCodeRecipe) parsing `docker compose config --format json` output from a fixture, and a `docker compose ... config -q` step in scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=x docker compose -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.identity.yml -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.claude-code.yml config -q` exits 0, and the same `config` output piped to `grep -c WARDEN_CP_TOKEN` prints 0.
- [ ] `go test ./test/deploy -run TestClaudeCodeRecipe` passes: `claude-code` is attached only to `claude-code-internal`, that network is `internal: true`, no volume of `warden-identity` or the CA key is mounted into `claude-code`, Dex and LDAP are not on `claude-code-internal`, and every third-party image is pinned by digest.
- [ ] With the stack up and the seeded user alice logged in, `docker compose exec claude-code claude -p 'say ok'` produces a worker decision for api.anthropic.com with decision allow, user_sub equal to alice's sub and act `claude-code`; with only the placeholder the upstream answer is 401, and with a real key on the worker the prompt completes (manual step in the doc).
- [ ] Running `up -d` a second time succeeds and creates no new agents, agent_keys, worker_tokens or worker_enroll_tokens rows.
- [ ] `docker compose exec claude-code env` contains no `sk-ant-` value and `grep -cE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'` over it prints 0.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` passes, including its secret-literal stage.

### 5/6 · W-P2-RCP-05

**Add the isolation proof script for the recipes**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#121](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/121)

Add scripts/recipe-isolation.sh, which proves for each recipe that the agent has no route out except the forwarder and the worker, holds no identity material or real vendor key, and is attributed to the logged-in user. It runs only on request through `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes`, follows the scripts/smoke-identity.sh pattern from W-P1-IDC-03, and needs no real vendor key.

**Requirements**

- `scripts/recipe-isolation.sh <claude-code|codex>` brings the merged stack up from a clean state, puts the seeded user's token from `scripts/dex-token.sh --raw alice` into the sidecar's `--subject-token-file` without passing it through argv or an echoed variable, and runs `docker compose down -v` in a trap.
- Checks from inside the agent container: direct-egress-blocked (`curl --noproxy '*' https://example.com` fails); idp-and-cp-unreachable (no TCP to dex:5556 or control-plane:7070, and the identity volume path is absent); forwarder-405 (a plain-HTTP request to warden-identity:3128 gets 405); no-secrets-in-agent (env, /proc/*/environ and $HOME contain no JWT-shaped string, no PEM private key and no vendor key other than the placeholder).
- Checks of attribution and policy: attributed-allow (a request to the allowed API host through the forwarder gets an upstream answer, 401 with the placeholder is fine, and the worker decision has decision allow, user_sub of alice and act equal to the agent id); policy-deny (a CONNECT to a non-allowed host is denied); cp-attribution (`GET /dashboard/api/traffic?user=<alice email>` returns the event with identity_status valid).
- Checks from a probe container on the worker network: no-token-407 (`curl -x http://warden:8080` with no credentials gets 407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="warden"`) and header-replaced (a client Proxy-Authorization sent through the forwarder does not reach the worker, shown by the attributed sub).
- agent-disabled: after `warden control-plane agent disable` with the offline CLI (W-P2-AREG-06), a new CONNECT through the forwarder is refused within 10s.
- no-token-in-logs: `grep -cE 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}'` over the script output and `docker compose logs` for the worker, warden-identity and the CP prints 0.
- Each check prints PASS or FAIL with its name; the script exits non-zero at the first failure after printing the worker's last 50 log lines with JWT-shaped strings redacted. It uses `set -euo pipefail`, no `set -x`, and finishes within 5 minutes per recipe on a warm image cache.
- `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes` runs both recipes; the default `scripts/check.sh` does not start Docker. docs/testing-guide.md documents the flag.

**Implementation plan**

1. New scripts/recipe-isolation.sh with a check() helper, the trap, the token hand-off and one function per check.
2. Add `--smoke-recipes` to the argument loop in scripts/check.sh next to `--integration` and `--smoke-identity`.
3. Add a temporary negative-test override deploy/compose/test/recipe-egress-leak.yml that also attaches the agent to egress, used only by the self-test.
4. Document the flag and the checks in docs/testing-guide.md and link it from both recipe docs.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `scripts/recipe-isolation.sh claude-code` and `scripts/recipe-isolation.sh codex` each exit 0 from a clean state and print PASS for direct-egress-blocked, idp-and-cp-unreachable, forwarder-405, no-secrets-in-agent, no-token-407, header-replaced, attributed-allow, policy-deny, cp-attribution, agent-disabled and no-token-in-logs.
- [ ] With the deploy/compose/test/recipe-egress-leak.yml override added, the script exits non-zero at direct-egress-blocked.
- [ ] With the served agent entry changed to `identity: attribute`, the script exits non-zero at no-token-407.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` without `--smoke-recipes` starts no Docker container and passes; `scripts/check.sh --smoke-recipes` runs both recipes.
- [ ] `shellcheck scripts/recipe-isolation.sh` exits 0.

### 6/6 · W-P2-RCP-06

**Extend `warden identity exec` with agent tokens and `--run-as`**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#272](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/272)

W-P1-IDC-04 ships `warden identity exec` in P1 with the user's Dex ID token. Add `--agent-id`, so exec injects an exchanged Warden token from W-P2-RCP-01 through the W-P2-RCP-02 forwarder (rotation drain, reason-coded 503s), and `--run-as`, so a child under another uid cannot read the agent key or identity cache. Document that a same-uid child can still read them without `--run-as`, and add the P2 addendum to docs/identity-contract.md.

**Requirements**

- `warden identity exec` (W-P1-IDC-04) gains `--agent-id ID` and `--run-as uid:gid`; all P1 flags, the per-run loopback credential, the child env rules, signal handling and exit codes are unchanged.
- With `--agent-id` the forwarder token comes from WardenTokenSource (W-P2-RCP-01) and uses the W-P2-RCP-02 rotation drain and 503 reasons; without it exec behaves exactly as in P1. No Warden token, Dex token or key path enters the child's env, argv or files.
- `--run-as uid:gid` (Linux only; an error elsewhere) starts the child under another uid through SysProcAttr.Credential so it cannot read the key file or cache. docs/recipes/README.md states that without it `exec` protects against leaks through env, argv and logs and against stale tokens, but not against a hostile same-uid child.
- On ErrExchangeDenied at start exec exits 4 without starting the child; ErrLoginRequired keeps the P1 behaviour (login on a terminal, otherwise exit 2).
- docs/identity-contract.md gets a P2 addendum describing `forward` and `exec --agent-id` for require-mode agents, with no change to any v1 header or claim.

**Implementation plan**

1. cmd/proxy/identity_exec.go (from W-P1-IDC-04): add the `--agent-id` and `--run-as` flags and select WardenTokenSource when an agent id is set.
2. SysProcAttr.Credential behind a linux build tag, with a clear error on other platforms.
3. Tests in cmd/proxy using the helper-process pattern: TestIdentityExecAgentToken, TestIdentityExecExchangeDenied, and a linux-only TestIdentityExecRunAs that skips when not root.
4. Write the docs/identity-contract.md addendum and the exec section in docs/recipes/README.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExecAgentToken` shows that with `--agent-id` the fake worker receives the exchanged Warden token, and the child's env and argv contain no substring of the Warden or Dex token.
- [ ] With the token endpoint returning invalid_client, `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExecExchangeDenied` shows exit 4 and that the child never started.
- [ ] On Linux as root, `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestIdentityExecRunAs` shows the child runs as the given uid and cannot open the agent key file; on other platforms `--run-as` exits non-zero before starting the child.
- [ ] The P1 TestIdentityExec cases from W-P1-IDC-04 pass unchanged, and `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-RCP-02`](identity-client.md#26--w-p2-rcp-02) Add the token-injecting forwarder and `warden identity forward`; [`W-P1-IDC-04`](identity-contract.md#44--w-p1-idc-04) Add `warden identity exec` with a loopback forwarder that refreshes the token
